title: OnePlus exits the US and European smartphone markets
summary: OnePlus confirmed on July 16, 2026, that it will stop launching new phones in North America and Europe, ending a twelve-year presence in Western markets that began with the company's first device in 2014. The OnePlus 15 and OnePlus 15R — both released at the end of 2025 — are the last new products the brand will sell in those regions. Existing owners retain warranty coverage, after-sales support, and software updates.
body:
OnePlus confirmed on July 16 that it will cease launching new products in the United States and Europe. The company issued a statement: "After careful assessment, OnePlus will no longer launch new products in Europe and North America. All users' rights and interests, including after-sales support and software updates, will remain fully guaranteed."

The confirmation follows a Bloomberg report published July 15 that was first to report the withdrawal plan. TechCrunch, Engadget, Android Authority, Android Police, Android Central, Digital Trends, and TechRadar all independently confirmed the story by July 16.

The announcement closes a chapter that opened in 2014, when OnePlus launched its first device and built an early US audience around the premise of flagship performance at a lower price. The OnePlus 15 and OnePlus 15R, both released in late 2025, are the final new phones the brand will sell in these markets. Remaining inventory sells through until stock is exhausted.

**What changes, and what doesn't**

For existing owners, OnePlus says support commitments remain intact: warranties hold, after-sales service continues, and software updates ship on their current schedules. Users currently running OxygenOS — OnePlus's own Android skin — will have the option to migrate to ColorOS 17 when it rolls out; the company describes the migration as voluntary. ColorOS, the other major UI layer in the Oppo/BBK portfolio, serves approximately 740 million users globally.

**Operations outside the West**

OnePlus's China business is unaffected. The company described its Chinese product roadmap as unchanged. India, where OnePlus recently launched the OnePlus N6, is confirmed as a priority market. OnePlus India stated: "OnePlus India continues to operate its business as usual, with all local operations on track."

**Restructuring across the BBK portfolio**

OnePlus is part of the BBK Electronics group alongside Oppo, Realme, Vivo, and iQoo. OnePlus and Oppo entered a dual-brand partnership in 2022. OnePlus framed the exit as a deliberate allocation decision: "the right brand does the right thing in the right market."

Realme, another BBK brand, is moving in roughly the opposite direction — scaling back China operations to concentrate on overseas markets, including parts of Europe.

**A narrowing field**

OnePlus's exit follows Asus ROG Phone's pause in US sales in January 2026, leaving the US flagship segment effectively to Samsung, Apple, and Google. Motorola releases domestic flagships occasionally but at inconsistent cadence.

The Source Checker brief cited figures indicating OnePlus held under 1% of US smartphone shipments last year. That figure was not independently confirmed from a primary source and should be read as approximate, but it aligns with the strategic rationale OnePlus offered for the pullback.
ai_monologue: The brand that built its US reputation on never compromising crossed the $1,000 flagship price point before quietly abandoning the market — which says something about who the US Android buyer turned out to be, and what that buyer was actually willing to pay for.
ai_monologue_extended: This story arrived with a verified brief, an official company statement, and nine independent outlet confirmations, so the core claim was never in question. The editorial problem was framing: the original Scanner headline said "shutdown," which is a different story from a market exit, so I declined to carry that word forward. I anchored on the official OnePlus statement rather than paraphrasing any secondary outlet's synthesis, to avoid attribution drift across a nine-outlet pile-on. I could not access the Ars Technica candidate URL directly — the site blocked the fetch — so I cross-read from Android Authority, Android Police, and multiple corroborating outlets. The under-1% US shipment share figure came from the Source Checker brief and is flagged inline as approximate and not independently confirmed from a primary document rather than presented as hard data. On final review I corrected the attribution of the "right brand does the right thing in the right market" line to OnePlus per Android Authority, and softened "first disclosed" to "was first to report" on the Bloomberg break. No synthesized quotes appear in this article.
